title: RAW development and qualification
objective: Make RAW development fast and simple — one tile executor on the shared pool, normalization in Rust, a GainMap without repeated weights, a measured source-cache policy, a narrow safe develop boundary, one container parser, a trimmed public API and tooling — and finish the qualification of continuous RAW editing for the Nikon Z6, Fujifilm X100VI and DJI Air 2S.
context_summary: Continuous RAW editing is implemented: LibRaw decodes a retained u16 mosaic, pinned librtprocess RCD and Markesteijn develop float planes, and one verified source cache with single-flight preparation keyed by gains feeds the renderer. The performance waves layered a process-wide scratch semaphore production cannot contend, a batch-and-barrier tile executor that idles the pool behind its tail job, and normalization written twice in C++ (parallel for Bayer, serial for X-Trans); history, compare and a second client each redevelop the one cached development. The RAW qualification milestone's tasks (controlled quality, the foundation and journey checkpoints, failure hardening, packaging, whole-editor measurement and RAW export) run beside the engineering waves. Decisions: docs/decisions.md "Post-consolidation review"; constraints: docs/design/post-consolidation.md; RAW contracts: docs/design/initial-raw.md, raw-integration.md, air2s-dng.md.

tasks.description: Delete the process-wide native scratch semaphore and its timed waits from `luxforge-raw`, keeping each development's own lane cap, and remove the semaphore's test lock and permit tests with it.
extra_context: Wave 1, fix. The semaphore is dead weight production cannot contend, and it is also a load-dependent test's only reason to exist; deleting it removes the failure class instead of patching one instance of it.

`native_tiles.rs` holds a static 8-slot semaphore (`SLOTS`, `admit`, `ScratchPermit`, `PEAK_SLOTS`, `TEST_BUDGET_LOCK`) with the RAW path's only timed waits: a 1 ms `park_timeout` loop for Rayon callers and a 20 ms timed condvar wait for everyone else. In production it can never block: `RawSource::develop` runs only on the single source worker, which already waits on the plane gate for every earlier development's planes to release before it starts the next, and each call already caps its own concurrency at 8 or fewer lanes.

`native_tiles::tests::rayon_waiter_runs_queued_permit_release_in_a_one_thread_pool` asserted `permit.count == MAX_SCRATCH_SLOTS` as 7 instead of 8 twice inside a full `cargo test --locked --workspace` run, and passed every time it ran alone. Its own `PEAK_SLOTS == MAX_SCRATCH_SLOTS` assertion only reads a process-wide high-water mark that the same test's first admission of all 8 slots already set, so it is unconditionally true and proves nothing about the executor.
Keep the per-call lane cap (8 today) and the plane gate that already serializes developments; only the global slot counter, its timed waits and its test-only lock go.

tasks.description: Replace the native tile executor's joined batches with one refill scope, also used by the Rust development passes, so no job waits for a batch's slowest one and at most eight tiles of work are ever open to stealing.
extra_context: Wave 3, speed. Once the semaphore is gone, the remaining scheduling cost is a serialized tail job plus joined batches, on every development.

The long dependent tail job runs inside the executor's first scope, so every other job waits for it; the remaining jobs then run in batches of at most 8, each batch joined before the next starts, so every batch waits for its slowest job. On the Z6 (RCD, 805 tiles, 110 jobs, a 38-tile tail) that models 36-49 ms against a measured 40.8 ms; on the X100VI (Markesteijn, 4,293 tiles, 562 jobs, a 162-tile tail) it models about 200-275 ms. A refill schedule is estimated at about 25-28 ms for the Z6 and 150-165 ms for the X100VI.

The same at-most-eight-tiles-of-stealable-work rule the executor exists for is not applied to the Rust passes that run on the same pool: DNG correction rows (`dng.rs`) and camera-conversion chunks (core `source.rs`) both run a plain adaptive parallel iterator over the whole frame instead.

Give every spawned task one job, then have it re-spawn itself to pull the next index from a shared counter; the caller runs the tail job first, then pulls ordinary jobs itself until none remain. Offer the same executor to the Rust passes, or record a measurement that justifies leaving them on a plain parallel iterator.
Cancellation between jobs and the tail's serial position both stay; every job still starts at a full tile with fresh scratch, so bytes cannot change.

tasks.description: Move RAW mosaic normalization and the post-demosaic /65535 scale into Rust on the development pool, so the native `lf_raw_develop` call only demosaics.
extra_context: Wave 3, speed. Normalization and the output scale are serial full-frame work on the single source thread today; moving them into Rust removes duplicated C++ and lets them run on the pool this plan just gave a refill schedule.

X-Trans normalization is never parallel in `adapter.cpp`: `normalize_rows` batches only when `meta->cfa_width == 2` (Bayer); X-Trans always takes the serial loop below it. The Bayer serial cost was measured at 39.5 ms at 24.5 MP, which projects to about 65-90 ms at the X100VI's 40.9 MP. Both loops divide `65535 / (white - black)` per pixel and re-check invariants `interpret` already validated at decode. `std::vector<float> mosaic(count)` zero-fills the normalized mosaic (491 MB on the X100VI) before either loop overwrites it, and a final serial loop divides all three planes by 65535 after the demosaic.
`neutral.rs` keeps a third copy of the same per-site black-level model, in f64, for the neutral picker.

Precompute the same per-site `black` and `65535.0 / (white - black)` values C++ computes per pixel, evaluate `(sample - black) * k * gain` in the same order for Bayer and X-Trans alike, and divide the planes by 65535 in parallel chunks as soon as the native call returns, still ahead of the DNG corrections so the order of operations is kept. The neutral picker reuses the site-to-black lookup instead of keeping its own copy.
Bytes must not change: keep the same IEEE f32 subtraction, division and multiplications in the same order, with no `a*b+c` shape a compiler could contract into an FMA.

tasks.description: Precompute the DNG GainMap's row and column weights once per row and column instead of recomputing them for every pixel and channel.
extra_context: Wave 3, speed. This is now the Air 2S's largest development stage, since pooled RCD already made the native demosaic itself fast.

`Warp::apply`'s per-pixel loop calls `GainMap::gain` once per stage, per channel, per pixel; on the Air 2S active area (5472x3648, about 20 million pixels) that is about 60 million calls. Each call re-derives `fy`, `y0` and `wy` from the row alone, and `fx`, `x0` and `wx` from the column alone, then re-does the same bounds checks, clamps and floors every time.

Precompute `(x0, x1, wx)` once per column and `(y0, y1, wy)` once per row for each stage, and evaluate the same bilinear expression per channel; keep `(pixel as f64 * gain) as f32` exactly as it is today.
Same f64 operands, same operations, same order: the corrected mosaic is byte-identical by construction, not by re-verification alone.

tasks.description: Evict the cached RAW development only when a queued task will allocate new planes, then measure the hold-`\` compare on the X100VI and add a byte-budgeted second slot or a proxy-only compare if a switch still costs more than about 150 ms.
extra_context: Wave 3, speed. The eviction rule costs whole redevelopments on ordinary Lightroom-familiar gestures; the owner's decision on a second development slot waits for this task's own measurement of what this plan's other RAW speedups leave behind.

`queue_preparation` and the completion path in the owner evict the cached development for any strict evaluation at other gains: selecting a history entry, holding `\` to compare against the Original (two redevelopments per toggle), or another client's sample or analysis of a different entry. Measured before this plan's speed work: Historical Original to captured frame p50 507 ms (Z6), 1,559 ms (X100VI), 1,484 ms (Air 2S); Return to current 491, 1,616, 1,523; a 100% view change costs about 25 ms by comparison on every camera. A completed source job also evicts a just-installed development whenever any other job is active, artifact-only reads included.

Memory (CPU bytes, at 18 B/px: u16 mosaic + f32 normalized mosaic + f32 planes): a development peaks at 441 MB on the Z6 and 736 MB on the X100VI; steady displayed is about 510/810 MB; a white-balance-release peak is about 0.61/0.97 GB. Two float developments never coexist; the plane gate enforces that and stays untouched. The crate's 128 MP pixel limit binds before its 1.5 GiB per-buffer limit; at that cap a development peaks at about 2.3 GB before any RGBA.

The owner's decision: keep one RAW development per process until this task and the executor and normalization changes land, then measure the hold-`\` compare on the X100VI; if a switch still costs more than about 150 ms, add a byte-budgeted second development slot (for example 600 MB or less) or a compare that shows only the other entry's proxy while the exact frame redevelops. A byte-budgeted cache that also keeps JPEG decodes beside the one RAW development follows only after a separate RSS measurement on the M4.

Fix the eviction rule regardless of which option follows the measurement: evict only when a queued task allocates new planes (a File or Develop job), not on every artifact-only job in the flight table.

tasks.description: Narrow the RAW develop FFI boundary to one safe crate-private wrapper taking an options struct, with generated status codes and no test or diagnostic hooks in the production ABI.
extra_context: Wave 4, structure. The decode half of the boundary is already minimal and stays as it is; only the develop half is wider than its job.

`lf_raw_develop` takes 17 positional arguments across 10 unsafe call blocks (1 production, 9 tests), each restating the same safety argument. Four forwarding wrappers (`develop`, `develop_uncorrected`, `develop_uncorrected_with_workers`, `develop_for_performance_diagnostic`) exist for three knobs: the worker limit, whether the executor runs, and a diagnostics pointer. Status codes 1-7 are literals on both sides of the boundary, matched by hand in Rust. Test and diagnostic hooks (a fault injector, a normalized-mosaic capture pointer) sit in the same signature production uses.

Add one crate-private `native_develop(&NativeDevelop) -> Result<(), RawError>` holding the only unsafe call, used by production and tests alike; add one `develop_with(options)` in place of the four-level chain; generate a status enum into the header `build.rs` already writes for the limits, mapped in one match.

With the previous task's normalization move, `lf_raw_develop` takes a small shape struct (dimensions, CFA kind and pattern, `rgb_cam`) instead of the full metadata box, which then serves only the decode call.

tasks.description: Parse every TIFF/DNG container with one IFD walk and one byte-reader set, merge the two opcode modules, share one 3x3 matrix helper, and parse DNG opcode lists only for DNG files.
extra_context: Wave 4, structure. Three walks over the same untrusted structure, each bounded slightly differently, are copies that drift apart; one walk is one set of bounds to get right.

`format.rs` walks IFDs three times (`dng_opcodes`, `dng_container`, `dng_color_calibration`), each with its own SubIFD-offset decoding, and the three do not agree on whether a zero offset or a zero SubIFD count is allowed. `dng_ops.rs` is a second, isolated module with its own error type (`OpcodeError`) and its own byte readers, adapted by `dng.rs` rather than sharing `RawError` and one reader set. "Required opcode IDs" (filter by the optional flag, collect, sort, dedup) is written three times: twice in `lib.rs` and once in `format.rs`. The same 3x3 cofactor-expansion determinant is written out four times: twice in `lib.rs`, once in `format.rs` and once in `profiles.rs`. DNG opcode lists are parsed for every TIFF-magic RAW file, NEF included, though only DNG needs them.

Write one `Tiff::walk(first, limit, |ifd, entries| ...)` with one bounds policy; merge `dng_ops.rs` into `dng.rs` on `RawError` and one reader set; write one `required_ids` helper; add a small `mat3` helper that `build.rs` includes the way it already includes `limits`, `opcodes` and `profiles`; gate opcode-list parsing on LibRaw reporting a DNG version.

This reorganizes the Rust-side parsing that already runs after LibRaw's own unpack; it does not touch or replace that unpack. Replacing LibRaw's unpack with RawSpeed is a separate proposal awaiting the owner and is out of scope here.

Malformed-input edge behavior (for example a zero SubIFD offset) may change where the three walks disagreed; every existing malformed-input case, in both the unit tests and the real-file suite, must still resolve the same way or fail explicitly, never silently.

tasks.description: Trim `luxforge-raw`'s public API to what the core and xtask actually use, and replace the generated 103-variant `RawMode` enum with a validated static reference.
extra_context: Wave 4, structure. A public surface wider than its consumers, and a generated enum matched on only as a string, are both maintenance cost with no behavior behind them.

`mosaic_arc` has no caller anywhere; `mosaic_corrections`, `corrected_sensor_sample_location` and `gain_at_corrected_sensor` are used only by in-crate callers or the real-file test suite; `required_dng_opcodes` is re-exported but used only by tests. The generated `RawMode` enum (103 variants across the 100-camera catalog) is used in production only through its serde form and `requires_dng_corrections`, which scans the catalog anyway; one call site builds a `RawMode` by writing its id as JSON and parsing it back.

Make the four functions crate-private, moving their real-file assertions into `dng.rs`'s own tests; replace the generated enum with `RawMode(&'static Mode)`, deserialized by catalog lookup, with `requires_dng_corrections` as a field on `Mode` instead of a generated match. The generated `raw_modes.rs` and the JSON round trip both go.

tasks.description: Delete `cargo xtask raw-corpus` and the finished RAW backend probes, and port or explicitly exempt the two remaining Python camera-addition tools.
extra_context: Wave 4, structure. Superseded tooling and finished experiments left in the tree cost maintenance and contradict the one-toolchain decision; `raw-editor` and `raw-panel` are still needed and keep their place.

`xtask/src/raw.rs`'s `raw-corpus` command (272 lines) runs in no verification tier, carries a stale 128 MiB source limit against the 512 MiB RAW bound, and is superseded: `raw-editor` already verifies each source's SHA-256 and `qualify_profiles` already hashes each source before and after. `probes/raw` (about 2,800 lines of Python and C++, plus a 1,373-line `Cargo.lock` for its own Rawler-based Rust workspace) mixes three finished backend-selection experiments (the Rawler crate, three C++ probes, `run.py`, `compare.py`) with two tools still used to add a camera (`dng_reference.py` and its JSON fixture, `collect_camera_metadata.py`); their Python contradicts the decision that all development tooling is Rust.

Delete `raw-corpus` and its usage/documentation references; delete the finished Rawler crate, the three C++ probes, `run.py` and `compare.py`; port `dng_reference.py` into an independent Rust reference crate and `collect_camera_metadata.py`'s workflow into xtask when it is next touched, or record an explicit exception to the one-toolchain rule in docs/decisions.md with a reason.

tasks.description: Measure full-editor RAW responsiveness, memory and JPEG regressions on the owner's M4.
extra_context: RAW qualification milestone on the roadmap, not a wave of the post-consolidation work.
This measurement is taken after the development executor and normalization changes land, so the recorded distributions describe the code that ships, not the code this plan's speed work replaces.
Provisional time/RSS targets are investigation hypotheses until the owner accepts measured budgets. Do not hide misses by changing input modes or quietly enabling embedded previews.

The implemented raw-editor command records whole-editor edit/history/reopen distributions and sampled process RSS. Fine-grained stage, GPU, cancellation and idle attribution remain separate outstanding work; JPEG baselines use editor-performance.

Thirty complete native M4 trials per owner camera and four public mode workflows pass. The same 24/60 MP JPEG core diagnostic is recorded before/after. Fuji captured RSS p95 is 1992 MiB with an unexplained 2436 MiB maximum; screenshot-free peaks are 1583-1647 MiB. Fine-grained stage/GPU/cancellation/idle attribution and an accepted budget remain open.

Measurement depends on the implemented editor, not on completion of broad controlled-scene/fuzz/portability gates. Those gates remain independently open. RSS sampling includes renderer/capture effects and must not be relabelled as isolated CPU heap or GPU memory.
